title: Restocking to a list
audience: Cleaners on short-stay, hotel-style and serviced-apartment turnovers who replenish guest items between stays.
learningOutcomes: Restock a room by working through the approved list in the room's layout order.
Check each item for presence, count, condition and expiry before it is placed.
Report a shortfall without substituting an item that is not on the approved list.

instruction.heading: Why restock against a list
instruction.body: Guests look for items and expect them in the places they know. A missing pen, an empty tea caddy or a set of glasses that is not set out is noticed on arrival, and it costs more trust than a guest would expect from so small an omission. A written list makes sure every item is checked in the same way for every room. Without a list, cleaners tend to restock what they remember and miss what they do not. The list is the record of what the room should contain.

instruction.heading: Working the list
instruction.body: Read the list in the order the room is laid out, not in the order items were used. For each item, check that it is present, counted, in good condition and within any expiry date. Replace anything damaged, expired or stained with approved stock. Keep clean items clean: handle glassware and mugs by the base or the rim, and keep tea and coffee materials sealed. Empty, clean and dry any container such as an ice bucket before refilling it from the approved supply. Tick each line only after the item is in place.

instruction.heading: Presenting the items
instruction.body: Position matters, because guests look at a room in a fairly set way. Place stationery, the information folder and menus where a guest first looks for them. Set glassware and mugs where the list places them. Do not overfill a shelf, and do not hide items inside drawers unless the list says so. Items for use, such as toiletries and laundry bags, go where a guest can reach them without moving other things.

instruction.heading: Shortfalls and substitutions
instruction.body: If an item on the list is short, do not replace it with a similar item from another room or from a personal supply. Record the shortfall with the item name and the room, and tell the coordinator so that stock can be refilled. A substitution is only made where the list names an approved alternative. Food and drink items follow the property's food-handling rules for storage and presentation.

procedure: Open the restock list for this property and this room type.
Check each item in the order it appears in the room layout: present, counted, in good condition and within any expiry date.
Replace any damaged, expired or stained item with approved stock.
Empty, clean and dry any container, such as an ice bucket, and refill it from the approved supply.
Place each item in its set position, both for use and for presentation.
Count the consumables that were used, and record any shortfall.
Tick each line only after the item is in place and checked.

workedExamples.situation: A serviced apartment's list includes two bottles of water, a pen, a notepad, laundry bags, tea and coffee sachets, and a menu folder. The laundry bags are at the bottom of the wardrobe, and the tea box is empty.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should you do about the empty tea box, and where do the laundry bags go?
workedExamples.reasoning: Take a full box from the approved stock and place it in its set position, then record the use on the list. If there is no approved stock, do not borrow from another room. Record the shortfall and tell the coordinator. Move the laundry bags to the set position so that a guest can find them without searching.

equipmentAndPpe: The restock list for the property
Cloths for cleaning containers and glassware
Gloves where the task requires them

commonErrors.error: Restocking from memory rather than from the list.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the list in order for every room.

commonErrors.error: Using a similar product that is not on the approved list.
commonErrors.prevention: Use approved items only, and ask the coordinator for an approved alternative.

commonErrors.error: Placing items wherever there is space, not where the guest looks for them.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the set positions on the list.

commonErrors.error: Ticking the list before the item has been placed.
commonErrors.prevention: Tick each line after the item is in place and checked.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Check the seal and expiry date on consumables before placing them. Do not place damaged or expired items in a room.
Restocking does not include purchasing, pricing or any change to the approved list. Those decisions sit with the business and the property.

qualityStandard: Every line on the list is ticked, and every item is in its set position.
No expired, damaged or stained item is left in the room.
No item has been borrowed from another room without a record.
documentationEvidence: Completed restock list for the room
Shortfall report with the item name and the room
summary: Restock from the list, in the order of the room layout, and tick only after each item is in place.
Use approved stock only, and report a shortfall rather than substituting.
Position items where the guest will look for them, not where space happens to be.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why use a written restock list?
options: So that every room is checked the same way, with no items missed
So that the list can replace the final walk-through
So that items can be bought in bulk at a lower cost

knowledgeChecks.question: A room's list calls for a tea box, which is empty, and there is no approved stock in the room. What do you do?
options: Take a box from the next room, because the rooms are the same and the stock is the same there
Record the shortfall and tell the coordinator, without substituting an unapproved item
Use a similar product from the kitchen if the coordinator agrees to it today

knowledgeChecks.question: When should a line on the restock list be ticked?
options: Before the item is placed, so the list is finished early
Once the item is in its set position and has been checked
At the end of the day, for all rooms together
